summary: A Reddit user, u/PopShort7064, asked the "Am I The A**hole?" forum whether she was wrong to agree to walk her daughter Calla down the aisle and do a mother/daughter dance instead of involving her husband, Calla's stepfather. Her husband felt hurt and believed she should have considered him or compromised. The post went viral, and most commenters defended the mother and bride, saying the stepfather should respect Calla's wishes and her bond with her late father.
one_line: A bride's mother was backed by Reddit commenters after agreeing to walk her daughter down the aisle, which upset her husband, the bride's stepfather.
key_facts: Reddit user u/PopShort7064 posted on the "Am I The A**hole?" forum about walking her daughter Calla down the aisle instead of her husband, Calla's stepfather.
The mother lost the father of her children, Calla and Hawthorn, when they were six and eight.
She remarried four years later, and her husband has been Calla's stepfather since Calla was 10.
The children's reaction to the new partner was strongly negative at first, so the family paused for a year and did therapy before things moved on.
The mother said her husband "was not going to be filling the role of a dad" and was fine with that as long as he was respected.
When Calla was 15, she told her mother she would want her to walk her down the aisle and to do a mother/daughter dance instead of a father/daughter one.
The mother planned to dance to the song Calla's dad used to sing to her.
When Calla got engaged, she asked her mother right away, and the mother said she would be honoured.
The husband asked whether Calla was asked about both parents walking her, whether she considered him, and whether the mother thought of him when she said yes.
The mother said she did not think of him because she was overjoyed; he said she should have given him more consideration and tried to compromise.
Three weeks after the incident, the husband had not changed his stance and felt he deserved more from the family.
The Reddit post received more than 6,500 upvotes, and many commenters defended the mother and criticised the stepfather.
One commenter said the real question was why the husband believed he was more entitled than the mother to the honour of walking Calla down the aisle.
